gamespot.com/articles/xbox-kept-at-least.title: Xbox Kept At Least One Big Promise In Its Most Tumultuous Year Ever
gamespot.com/articles/xbox-kept-at-least.excerpt: When it drastically increased the price of Game Pass Ultimate on October 1, 2025, Xbox made a promise in a now-deleted Xbox Wire post: “Ultimate subscribers now get access to over 75 day-one releases a year.” In the year since, a lot has changed at Xbox. It has hired a new CEO, laid off thousands of developers, spun off several studios, and scaled back its multiplatform plans. This past year has been one of pivots and changes in strategy for Xbox, so I wondered if that day-one release commitment for Game Pass Ultimate fell by the wayside. Over the past year, I have tracked every title added to Game Pass Ultimate the day it launched. As of Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy’s launch on August 27, 2026, Xbox has met the goal it set for Game Pass Ultimate content last year. Xbox looks very different now than it did a year ago, though, so reflecting on the past year of Game Pass Ultimate also means reflecting on what else has changed at Xbox over that time. This promotional image from October 2025 promotes "75+ day one games a year" as an Xbox Game Pass Ultimate benefit October 2025: 9 Games Added Sopa: The Tale of the Stolen Potato Little Rocket Lab Ball X Pit Keeper Ninja Gaiden 4 The Outer Worlds 2 Powerwash Simulator 2 Bounty Star: Super Fantasy Kingdom Following the price-increase announcement and 75+ game commitment, Xbox came out swinging in October. This was the busiest month in terms of first-party and second-party releases on the service over the past year, as Keeper, Ninja Gaiden 4, and The Outer Worlds 2 were all published by Xbox Game Studios. The Xbox ROG Ally also released this month and was positioned as a portable PC tailor-made for Game Pass. Fans and former Xbox developers did not take too kindly to the Game Pass Ultimate price hike, though, which turned what could’ve been a triumphant month for Xbox into one of controversy. gamespot.com/articles/minecraft-mobs-arr.title: Minecraft Mobs Arrive As Cookie Treats At Crumbl For Limited Time
gamespot.com/articles/minecraft-mobs-arr.excerpt: Chicken cookies! Crumbl has revealed a Minecraft collaboration that introduces six different desserts based on the sandbox game to the menu starting today. Yes, they're all square shaped, and no, there isn't a chicken jockey. Available tomorrow, August 31, through September 5, the four-sided treats include a cookie butter cookie with a chicken topper, a Creeper Key lime sandwich, and a lemon poppyseed cookie topped with a boxy bee. Those three treats are joined by an Enderman cookies-and-cream sandwich, which has purple marshmallow mousse in the middle. Who knew those weirdos could have such a tasty-sounding filling? Meanwhile, the pig-themed dessert is a cherry blossom cookie, with maraschino cherries and cherry cream cheese frosting as two of the key ingredients. Last but not least, there's a grass block cake that features a cinnamon vanilla base, brown cream cheese frosting, and lawn-textured frosting. These special Minecraft treats will be available at Crumbl from August 31 through September 5. The partnership doesn't stop there, either. Crumbl notes that there will be Minecraft mystery spoons, with a special exclusive one for the first 200 people who pick up a six-pack of the crossover cookie treats. Minecraft is not a new kid on the block when it comes to crossovers. Bluey came to the hugely popular game earlier this year, and there have been Minecraft Crocs available in the past. This new collaboration with Crumbl follows Krispy Kreme offering up special Pokemon doughnuts . gamespot.com/articles/get-the-entire-des.title: Get The Entire Destiny 2 Experience At 75% Off For A Short Time
gamespot.com/articles/get-the-entire-des.excerpt: Bungie may have stopped development on Destiny 2 , but that doesn’t mean that it’s over. Like the first game, its servers are still live and fairly active, and with Destiny 2’s excellent expansions, there are hundreds of hours of content waiting for both New Lights and returning Guardians to enjoy. As someone who has bought every expansion at release, seeing the entire Destiny 2 collection at 75% off is a remarkable deal, and one that I wholly recommend. I’ve got over 2,000 hours across both Destiny games, making them my second- and third-most-played games behind Minecraft. Even 12 years later, I still look back on the original fondly, and I’ve been a day-one player of both entries. It’s hard to put into words what makes Destiny so special, but I’ve got plenty of explanations for why Destiny 2 is one of the best FPS games ever–and why this deal shouldn’t be overlooked. You play as a Guardian (basically a superpower "Light"-wielding, gunslinging space wizard/warrior/assassin, depending on the class you pick). After being revived by the ever-present Traveler, you need to kill a bunch of bad guys. However, while you slay hordes of Hive, deal with the villainous Vex, or, well, the rest of the solar system’s enemies, you’ll uncover universe-spanning mysteries. The lore is deep, but you don’t have to go deep into it to have a good time; it’s definitely exciting if you decide to. While Destiny 2 itself is free-to-play (so you can go try it and see if you like it first), the expansions add a ridiculous amount of content, and personally, I wouldn’t play it without them anymore. Beyond Light adds the Darkness, the counterpart to the Light that powers Guardians, as the energy source for a new character subclass, while the excellent The Witch Queen sees you deal with Savathûn, one of the Hive gods, voiced by the brilliant Debra Wilson. gamespot.com/articles/aggressively-selli.title: “Aggressively” Selling PS5s Isn’t Needed, As Sony Focuses On Making More From Existing Owners
gamespot.com/articles/aggressively-selli.excerpt: This November will mark the sixth anniversary of the PlayStation 5 console's launch, but in the years since its arrival, the gaming market has changed dramatically. The trend of consoles becoming cheaper over time has vanished this generation, as the PS5 now costs more today than it did in 2020, and the expectation is that Sony's hardware sales could slow down over time. Sony doesn't seem too worried about that, as company president and CEO Hiroki Totoki explained that there's no need to "aggressively" sell the console. "We are in the latter half of the lifetime cycle of a PS console," Totoki said to the Wall Street Journal. "That means that we do not need to aggressively sell the console today. And rather than that, we're focusing on recurring revenue from the current user base. And already, PS Plus has more than 125 million MAU (monthly active users) today. And how to monetize from the users is quite important for us." https://youtu.be/obR5p5AzR_s Totoki wasn't clear by what he meant exactly in terms of aggressive PS5 sales, although it likely comes down to Sony not needing to discount the console or even sell it at a loss to draw in new users. Sony has been pretty open about its plans to increase revenue from the players it does have, and these numbers have been growing steadily over the last couple of years. PlayStation Plus is required to access online services for the vast majority of games available on the console, while higher tiers tempt potential subscribers with access to an expanded library of games via the PS Plus Game Catalog. At the same time, Sony is preparing to move toward an all-digital future , as over 80% of games purchased for the console are done so through its digital storefront. Once Sony begins to phase out game discs starting January 2028, plugging that gap should result in a sizable jump in its profits . gamespot.com/articles/fable-reboots-main.title: Fable Reboot’s Main Story Is About 20 Hours Long, Dev Says
gamespot.com/articles/fable-reboots-main.excerpt: The upcoming Fable reboot from developer Playground Games will have a main story that should take about 15-20 hours to complete, the developers have stated. However, as with any game, your mileage may vary, and Playground believes the new Fable game can be played forever if players want to. Associate game director Will Kennedy told Polygon , "We have around 15-20 hours of mainline quest gameplay." He added that the game has another 15-20 hours worth of "side and open-world exploration content gameplay." "And then, of course, the life systems are limitless, so you can play them for as long as you want," he added. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M79EnEkZ-cc Associate game director Craig Littler, meanwhile, added, "You can literally play it forever if that's what you want to do." The Fable reboot launches in February 2027. It was originally scheduled to launch in 2026, but Playground delayed it to 2027 to avoid a "chaotic window," and we all know that means GTA 6. Gameplay combat footage from Fable emerged online recently from Gamescom, and it looked rough, but GameSpot’s own hands-on time with the game told a different story . Fable launches February 23, 2027 for Xbox Series X|S, PS5, and PC.

gamespot.com/articles/for-street-fighter.title: For Street Fighter’s Chun-Li, Callina Liang Had To Get Her Thighs In Fighting Shape
gamespot.com/articles/for-street-fighter.excerpt: There are certain non-negotiable constants in the world of Street Fighter, from Ryu throwing Hadoukens to Dhalsim being referred to as "Stretchy-Arm Guy" by new players, and when it comes to Chun Li, the Interpol agent always has a set of thighs strong enough to crack a titanium-plated watermelon in half. October's Street Fighter movie looks like a faithful adaptation of the classic fighting games, and Chun-Li actress Callina Liang worked hard to get her body--especially her legs--into fighting shape for the role. To prepare for the part, Liang practiced several martial arts built around kicking techniques, but most importantly, she also switched to a high-protein diet to help bulk up her muscles. This was a tough program for Liang to follow--eating a dozen eggs every day had her on the verge of throwing up--but by the end of her training, she'd added an impressive layer of muscle to her thighs alone. "Chun-Li is all kicks. So we did a bunch of Taekwondo training, Muay Thai, and Wushu (Kung Fu)," Liang said to Empire Magazine (via IGN ). "I did two hours of that a day and strengthened my legs a lot and changed my diet drastically. When I was bulking, I ate 12 eggs a day. Every two hours, I had to have a meal, and I was on the verge of throwing up. But it worked. By the end of the shoot, my thighs had grown six-and-a-half centimeters each." https://youtu.be/Xt4X4FvXk2A Liang added that she prepared herself mentally by downloading multiple Street Fighter games onto her PlayStation 5, recording her moves in slow motion, and then playing them back so she could study them. Thighs are a particularly tough muscle group to train because they're designed to be high-endurance parts of the body. What this means is that they require extreme systemic fatigue and precise, agonizingly hard sets to properly grow over time--a process that is anything but easy. gamespot.com/articles/resident-evil-coul.title: Resident Evil Could Have Its Biggest Opening Weekend Ever With Its New Movie
gamespot.com/articles/resident-evil-coul.excerpt: Weapons director Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie hits theaters on September 17, and analysts predict it will set a record for the franchise. While the majority of the live-action movies turned a decent profit off of a relatively small budget, Cregger's take on the IP is currently projected to have the best opening weekend by a comfortable margin. That's according to the official publication of the National Association of Theater Owners, Box Office Pro. The survival-horror movie is predicted to bring in between $40 and $50 million in its North American opening weekend, which would be almost double Resident Evil: Afterlife's $26.6 million weekend from way back in 2010. The new Resident Evil movie also has a brisk running time of around 95 minutes, so that should allow theater owners to screen the film several times a day to maximize ticket sales. If Resident Evil does hit that $40 million or more mark, it'll be on par with the opening weekend of his last release, Weapons. The 2025 film made $43.5 million at its debut and went on to earn an impressive $270 million at the global box office. If the predictions are on the money, Cregger's Resident Evil will perform a lot better than 2021's Resident Evil: Welcome to Raccoon City, which was a box office bomb that made only $42 million during its theatrical run. But can Resident Evil maintain its momentum past the opening weekend? It's not unusual for movies to lose gas quickly after the first week, but Cregger's films generally tend to have long legs. 2016's Resident Evil: The Final Chapter is currently the best-performing Resident Evil movie with a global box office haul of $312.2 million. gamespot.com/articles/trust-us-were-reme.excerpt: Fear not, Control fans: Control Resonant will be packed with lore despite the combat-heavy trailers we've seen so far, according to developer Remedy. The lack of focus on story in promotional footage, says Remedy senior communications manager Miika Huttunen, is no reflection of the game's content, but instead a deliberate decision by the team to have the narrative side of the game on lockdown until release. In short: You'll get your fill, you just have to wait. The sneak peeks we've had of the game so far have been mainly combat-focused, a result of combat being something that doesn't need to be revealed gradually to the player. "There's lots of weird stuff to come," says Huttunen, "plenty of twists and turns and surprises… things to discover. We're asking fans to trust us--we're Remedy. And I hope that, because we're Remedy, we get the benefit of the doubt." Dialogue with NPCs, collectibles, and environmental clues will all give fans a new story to piece together. Lore-related collectibles, like FBC documents and written materials from pre-Hiss-invasion times, are scattered liberally throughout the game. It pays to explore and take your time finding secrets, as the world of Control Resonant is no less carefully crafted than its predecessor, and the story is far from an afterthought. Besides the written word, you'll also find countless places where you can open shortcuts, unpack subtle environmental clues, and have interactions with NPCs who help to expand your understanding of the world. Huttunen also revealed that Control Resonant will reward players' decisions in dialogue through subtle changes in how other characters react to them, side quest variations, and a slow build of their own personality. The main story will be largely linear and have one distinct ending--though if Remedy's track record is anything to go by, one that players won't see coming. We already know that you can preload the game a week before launch , but is that because you'll need multiple days to download all the files? GTA 6 fans are currently speculating just how big the install is going to be, with the majority of people taking part in a ResetEra poll guessing that it'll clock in between 100GB to 250GB. That's a fairly generous margin--and highly likely--given the history of Rockstar's previous games and the current state of game-install sizes. Considering that GTA 6 is a download-only game --physical copies are just a code in a box--you're going to want to make some space available on your PS5 or Xbox Series X|S. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XpPpqZwUwl0 For example, Red Dead Redemption 2 requires approximately 105GB to 150GB, depending on your platform, and was released in 2018. Video games have only gotten bigger and even more detailed since then, leveraging the power of modern hardware to create detailed worlds. High-resolution graphic textures and detailed character models only add to the install-size bloat, with some games even offering options to reduce that digital footprint by selectively installing parts of the experience. Call of Duty was a prime example, as the game typically offers an option to install it piecemeal . Modern Call of Duty games used to be up to 150GB in size, and once you started slotting in extra content like the Call of Duty HQ unified launcher, shared texture packs for older titles, Call of Duty: Warzone, and carry-forward content, the install size neared 300GB. gamespot.com/articles/us-senators-say-di.title: US Senators Say Discord And Roblox Should Have Their Day In Court
gamespot.com/articles/us-senators-say-di.excerpt: Three US Democratic senators condemned both Discord and Roblox, saying that the voice-chat and game-creation platforms "deserve their day in court" instead of hiding behind private arbitration methods as it relates to child safety. According to an August 31 Bloomberg report , Democratic senators Dick Durbin (Illinois), Kirsten Gillibrand (New York), and Richard Blumenthal (Connecticut) have filed an amicus brief on August 28 urging the courts to keep the myriad lawsuits Discord and Roblox are facing public. "Instead of hiding behind the veil of arbitration, Roblox and Discord can be held accountable for their misconduct: misleading parents into thinking their platforms are safe and failing to protect children from sexual abuse," the senators wrote collectively. "Such a requirement would contradict the very concern animating the EFAA in the first place: Companies enforce arbitration to silence and deny justice to survivors of sexual assault and sexual harassment." Arbitration is a way for lawsuits to get settled privately and outside of a regular courtroom. This would mean that, if Discord and Roblox compelled their victims into arbitration, whatever the aftermath of the lawsuits were would likely be sealed and unknown to the public. These senators don't want that to happen, specifically because of the Ending Forced Arbitration of Sexual Assault and Sexual Harassment Act Congress enacted in 2022, which blocks companies facing sexual abuse lawsuits from entering arbitration. The amicus brief (which is a document filed by someone who wants to give the courts extra information) was filed in a case involving a 13-year-old boy who reportedly met a predator on Roblox and was groomed, coerced, and blackmailed into sending lewd materials over Discord. This is just one of the hundreds of lawsuits both platforms are currently battling. gamespot.com/articles/metroid-created-th.title: Metroid Created The Formula, But Now It Faces The Same Uphill Battle As Everyone Else
gamespot.com/articles/metroid-created-th.excerpt: The original Metroid and Castlevania both turn 40 years old this fall. As the two series most responsible for creating the "metroidvania," we're taking this occasion to take a comprehensive view of the popular genre. This is Metroidvania Week . Samus steps into a room she has seen before. She has just regained the Morph Ball ability, opening a path that was previously out of reach, and turns around to retrace her steps. Then the door slams shut and a massive humanoid drone corners her. The familiar room becomes a trap as the bounty hunter scrambles to remember the layout, find an escape route, and survive an enemy she can't yet defeat. It's a perfect example of how Metroid Dread takes one of the defining ideas of the metroidvania genre, returning to places you've already explored, and makes it feel dangerous again. For nearly 40 years, Metroid has built its identity around backtracking, but Nintendo has been backtracking into the genre it helped create. The metroidvania formula has spent decades evolving beyond its origins, forcing Nintendo to find new ways to keep up with the games it inspired. The genre explosion has created a challenge for Nintendo. Its familiar characters and usually stellar gameplay design are not enough to stand out among the many metroidvanias that have emerged over the years. The company is no longer defining the genre so much as competing within it, forcing Metroid to find new ways to make its decades-old formula feel fresh. Hollow Knight is one of the most acclaimed modern metroidvanias Nintendo's Yoshio Sakamoto, one of Metroid's original creators, has watched this transformation happen from the beginning. In a 2021 interview with CNET, he acknowledged the abundance of games in the metroidvania genre and expressed gratitude for the developers who took Nintendo's ideas and made them their own. gamespot.com/articles/the-metroidvania-g.title: The Metroidvania Genre Owes Credit To Much More Than Castlevania And Metroid
gamespot.com/articles/the-metroidvania-g.excerpt: The original Metroid and Castlevania both turn 40 years old this fall. As the two series most responsible for creating the "metroidvania," we're taking this occasion to take a comprehensive view of the popular genre. This is Metroidvania Week . Since their inception 40 years ago, fate has intertwined the extraterrestrial exploits of Samus Aran and the Belmont family’s fiend-fighting over multiple generations. Both the Metroid and Castlevania series would become synonymous with one of gaming’s defining genres, reducing many complex mechanics to a simple portmanteau: the metroidvania. However, even before the fateful years of 1994 and 1997--the release years of Super Metroid and Castlevania: Symphony of the Night, respectively--several key mechanics integral to metroidvanias would first appear elsewhere, and not always where you’d expect. So in this brief history, we will look at these origins and how it has evolved not just in the late 1980s, but also more recent pivotal innovations that revolutionized the gaming industry. Let’s begin with what I would call "protovanias:" those that introduced one or two elements the metroidvania genre would later adopt. The earliest exploration platformer was Aztec for the Apple II computer in 1982, which has players exploring a temple with an Indiana Jones-inspired character. It’s a fairly loose inspiration, sure, but Japanese developers would soon combine this exploration gameplay with the popular RPGs such as Wizardry . Three years later, the PC-880 and other Japan-only PCs would get Xanadu: Dragon Slayer 2 . It’s the first-to-market game with 2D side-scrolling real-time RPG combat that requires backtracking and promotes non-linear exploration. Of course, history rightfully forgets Xanadu, as playing it today requires a Master’s degree in the arcane arts to understand. gamespot.com/articles/welcome-to-gamespo.title: Welcome To GameSpot Metroidvania Week
gamespot.com/articles/welcome-to-gamespo.excerpt: Metroidvanias. What was once a relatively niche genre has slowly become one of the most prolific across the industry. Through a combination of indie developers paying homage to their favorite classics and major publishers injecting search-action DNA into their top franchises, the genre centered around discovery and exploration has never been more thriving. The original Metroid was released in Japan on August 6, 1984. The original Castlevania was released in Japan on September 26, 1984. Metroid created the genre. Castlevania adopted and revitalized it with Symphony of the Night. Both give the genre its namesake. So this week, at the midpoint between these momentous anniversaries, seemed like a great time to mark the occasion with a closer look at the metroidvania genre. All week we'll be putting up fresh perspectives at all aspects of metroidvanias, so stick around for 100% completion. gamespot.com/articles/mortal-shell-2-upd.excerpt: Developer Cold Symmetry continues to tinker with Mortal Shell 2 , recently dropping a massive update that makes some substantial changes to its latest souls-like action-RPG. Alongside buffing certain weapons and fixing some glitches, the team has also addressed the game's greedy economy by making a few finite resources more plentiful around the world. Released on August 29, Mortal Shell 2's Week 1 Update makes some of the game's heaviest weapons stronger to compensate for their slowness. For example, the Obsidian Hammer hits way harder, and The Great Martyr's Blade had its damage output increased to make up for this change missing in the last patch . Overall, Cold Symmetry said that heavier weapons deal way more damage and poise now. The headlining feature, though, is the overhaul to the economy. Before this patch, Glimpses (a currency used to upgrade your shells ) and Tarcores (a currency used to upgrade your Tarstones ) were incredibly limited in the world. With this new patch, however, both currencies are much more plentiful in the game. To start, Tarcores are easier to collect now through a new set of items known as Fragile Tarstones. These pieces of equipment break after their durability depletes and, once broken, they yield Tarcores so you can upgrade your favorite Tarstones to their max levels more reliably. Glimpses are the same. There's a similar Glimpse Stone that, once shattered, gifts you some Glimpses to max out whatever shell you're maining or interested in. Although Mini-Beacons no longer reward you with Glimpses, you can get some by interacting with the Gloom Siphon at the Marrow Keep after collecting Ova. A keen strategist and a self-proclaimed master of war, I think it's Musashi's art that hits more keenly than his katana: it's minimalist, monochromatic, a study of nature defined by its simple brilliance. Less is more. Whether intentional or not, I think Capcom may have internalised this philosophy when creating Onimusha: Way of the Sword - a game based loosely on the life and conquests of Musashi. Seldom over-complicated and often composed with artisanal skill, Way of the Sword takes the philosophies of 16th Century Japan's most influential martial artist and somehow applies them to video game development. He was, predictably, cowering in a corner of the cave complex. Right, now to get out of here and claim a lifetime supply of partially decayed vegetation. Wait, what was that noise? I’ll not spoil the rest of the quest, but suffice it to say that it provided the first taste of Rebel Wolves’ vampire RPG offering the same sort of memorable adventure as the series many of its devs cut their teeth on - CD Projekt’s Witcher and Cyberpunk games. nintendolife.com/reviews/nintendo-switch.excerpt: Dawn of a new dream. There’s a lot riding on Onimusha: Way of the Sword . Capcom has a few dormant franchises in its dusty closets just waiting to be revived, yet this one feels particularly significant. Despite never really taking off commercially, Onimusha commanded a passionate fanbase that continues to hold the series in the highest regard – right up there with the likes of Resident Evil and Devil May Cry . So to bring back Onimusha with a brand-new mainline entry in 2026 — two decades after the last game — feels especially risky, but it’s one that I’m happy to report has largely paid off. I love Way of the Sword. It’s a wonderfully paced adventure that combines horror, action, exploration, and a surprising amount of comedy to great effect. gamespot.com/articles/godzilla-remaster-.title: Godzilla Remaster Devs Explain Why They Aren’t Worried About Releasing Near GTA 6
gamespot.com/articles/godzilla-remaster-.excerpt: Most upcoming games have looked to steer clear of the behemoth that is Grand Theft Auto 6 and avoid the month of November entirely. The upcoming remaster of 2002's Godzilla Destroy All Monsters Melee is a notable exception , and as it turns out, the developers didn't think about GTA 6 at all when choosing its release date. In an interview with IGN , senior designer at developer Pipeworks Simon Strange revealed GTA's looming release of November 16 wasn't a factor when choosing Godzilla Destroy All Monsters Melee: Remastered's November 3 release date. Like others online, the development team got a kick out of kaiju fans celebrating the fact that the King of the Monsters (and Barbie) were the only two pop culture icons brave enough to face off against developer Rockstar's open-world juggernaut. "Honestly, [it] wasn't even in our heads at all when we were picking the release date," Strange said. "That's not my business. I make the video games. I'm not too worried about when they come out. If Atari had come to us and said, 'Wow, we can't because we think it's going to affect the sales with GTA', we would've had that discussion. But no one ever said anything." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZBDD_Q9rSiQ As Strange points out, November 3 is a special date for the Godzilla fandom. It was on that same day in 1954 that the original Gojira film was released and is regarded as Godzilla's official birthday. Strange said the upcoming remaster arriving on the same day was "respectful," and that at the end of the day, Godzilla fans would show up no matter when it was released. "I wasn't looking at the calendar and being worried in any way, or thinking about what other games are coming out because the Godzilla fans are very excited for it," Strange said. "They'd buy it on any day that it came out, and putting it out on Godzilla's birthday, that's just respectful." gamespot.com/articles/this-new-roguelike.title: This New Roguelike Wants To Make Its Difficulty More Welcoming
gamespot.com/articles/this-new-roguelike.excerpt: Murals might look like a stylish take on the Hades roguelike formula at first glance, but Disney Illusion Island developer Dlala Studios isn't aiming to copy Supermassive's homework. Instead, the studio is looking to put its own spin on the genre , as it fuses dark fairy tales and hews closer to the action-first approach of modern-day Doom and Diablo. One other big difference in Murals is that it'll offer a customizable approach to difficulty, as Dlala Studios says it wants to prioritize player fun over punishing runs--unless you're into that kind of thing. "There are difficulty selectors, and you can kind of tweak some of the individual settings," Dlala CEO, Aj Grand-Scrutton, said to GameSpot. "We've kind of got some of the high-level ones you'd imagine: enemy damage, enemy health. We've also got stuff that affects the player's health. Something that [design director] Grant Allen was really keen on in Disney Illusion Island, we tried to make it as welcoming as possible. "And whilst this is obviously a slightly more core genre, we tried to do the same here. When we're building, we don't care about player deaths. Our goal isn't to kill the player; it's to make sure they have fun. We try to make it as customizable as we can so everyone can get through. Even if you're a button-masher, that's a legitimate tactic in our rules." https://youtu.be/D42nkf8EHMk Grand-Scrutton added that the moment-to-moment gameplay of roguelikes like Hades inspired the fast, frantic combat in Murals, but the goal was to capture a "persistent, linear" experience within the fairy tale worlds that players will explore. As mentioned above, Doom and Diablo also helped inspire the game's design, and Allen added that an indie game called Blazing Beaks also served as an influence. "For me, it was kind of like looking at those games and understanding the experimentation that they had," Allen added. gamespot.com/articles/xbox-game-pass-in-.title: Xbox Game Pass In September Expands With 7 New Games
gamespot.com/articles/xbox-game-pass-in-.excerpt: It's the start of a new month, and right on cue, Microsoft has revealed the first wave of games coming to Xbox Game Pass in September. The upcoming batch isn't too massive, but it does include a day-one release that competitive gamers will want to check out, along with more titles for Xbox Game Pass Premium. Inversely, Game Pass will be losing some pretty big titles this month, with Cyberpunk 2077 leading the wave of departures. Kicking things off today is Shelldiver, an incremental game about a turtle fishing for jellyfish and then selling its catch at its adorable little store. On September 3, Speedrunners 2 launches as a day-one game. This competitive co-op platformer now supports up to eight players online, and you'll need to outrun and outjump your rivals to win each match. I hope you have good memorization skills for the challenging levels! On September 4, Game Pass Premium subscribers can grab Dice a Million for some roguelike deck-building fun, and one of the big highlights in September is the inclusion of Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War on September 8. While new Call of Duty games won't be added to Game Pass on day-one, you can grab this 2020 first-person shooter and enjoy a tightly paced Cold War-era story centered around hunting down a Soviet agent who is looking to destabilize the world. Another roguelike deck builder joins Game Pass on September 10 in the form of the medieval-themed The Royal Writ, but if you'd prefer to bang knuckles, Virtua Fighter 5 R.E.V.O. World Stage is a pretty fun brawler featuring Sega's fighting game royalty, and it's available the same day. Rounding things out for the first half of September is RuneScape: Dragonwilds, a co-operative survival adventure. gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-removes-the-.title: GTA 6 Removes The Series’ Worst Feature
gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-removes-the-.excerpt: If you've played a Grand Theft Auto game before, then you are probably familiar with the series' sprinting mechanic. Rather than clicking the left analog stick like in most other games, you have to either hold or mash a face button. It's annoying, less intuitive, and feels like a relic of the past, and luckily, Rockstar apparently agrees: Grand Theft Auto 6 is doing away with it. As shared by the Italian YouTuber MikeShowSha , you will now click the analog stick in order to sprint. It's a welcome change for muscle memory if nothing else, as anything other than clicking the analog stick feels odd in 2026. We've occasionally seen other game series, like Halo, adjust control schemes over time to fit more modern standards, though usually the option for the old-style controls is available in these cases. Of course, this change is certainly the reason it took 13 years for Grand Theft Auto 6 to arrive. Other, less-important changes include a map that is three times bigger than Red Dead Redemption 2, a new Criminal Profile system, throwable dog poop, and a physical-fitness system. Grand Theft Auto 6 arrives November 19 for Xbox Series X|S and PS5, and it's expected to be one of the biggest entertainment launches in history. With the change to how you sprint, it just might get there.

gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-studio-on-ma.title: GTA 6 Studio On Massive Pressure: “We Are Nervous”
gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-studio-on-ma.excerpt: GTA 6 is one of the most-anticipated entertainment releases ever, and many experts agree that it's sure to be a fast success. However, Rockstar North boss Rob Nelson said the studio is "nervous" about the game's upcoming release and living up to 13 years worth of hype and expectations . "I try not to think about it," Nelson told IGN . "You’re aware of it, of course. But I think we just have to try and make something that we feel is innovating on what we've done previously, evolving it while still making it feel familiar." Nelson went on to say that external pressure on Rockstar to deliver a great game with GTA 6 does not compare to "the pressure we put on ourselves as a team." "Everyone wants things to be perfect. We are nervous! Nervous, of course, but also excited to see how people respond to this video and then ultimately the game," he said. "It is definitely a step forward in all respects for us--the size of the world, and how deep it feels. It’s a bit of a shock when you get in there, and you see the density of the traffic, the density of population, and the fidelity of their responses to you." Part of the reason why GTA 6 took so long to come to market is because Rockstar is "creating perfection," according to Rockstar owner Take-Two. Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick explained that Rockstar prioritized polish over rushing the game to release. “We’re seeking perfection,” he said. “When we feel we’ve optimized creatively, that’s the time to release.” “There’s inherent tension, potentially, between getting something to market and creating perfection,” Zelnick added. “But this company errs on the side of perfection.” GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. A report said the game might make enough money from preorders alone– amounting to an estimated $2 billion by launch –to pay for the game’s entire production budget.

gamespot.com/articles/chronicles-medieva.title: Chronicles: Medieval Provides An Impressive Sandbox For Players To Write Their Own History
gamespot.com/articles/chronicles-medieva.excerpt: Chronicles: Medieval is a sandbox RPG that puts players in the commanding role of a medieval army, providing a strong mix of action and strategy. GameSpot was able to preview a hands-off demo and speak with senior game designer Gareth Bourn and lead producer Sam Millen about this ambitious medieval sandbox experience set in 14th-century Europe, where there is an exciting amount of freedom and an impressive attention to detail. https://youtu.be/60uz4iicAig?si=CZyz_U6--73lOB8g Developer Raw Power Games has created a massive action-strategy game, which features large-scale tactical battles and real-time combat. The game is set during the age of the Hundred Years' War, and while the developer spent a lot of time researching for historical accuracy, this is not a game about reenacting history. Chronicles: Medieval is designed to give players access to a historically accurate sandbox in order to create their own history within the time period. "It's very important for us that there is room for sandbox and very expressive gameplay," Millen said. "The world and the troops within it give player[s] expression, so you can make combinations and tactical choices." Chronicles: Medieval has a rags-to-riches narrative, where the player starts with almost nothing and must work to build up their army and reputation. The game features a vast explorable map for regions of 14th-century Europe, and this allows players to discover camps, interact with NPCs, recruit new soldiers, and more. The map is covered in the fog of war, so players will need to explore to unlock more opportunities across the regions. The exploration map There is a lot of army management in Chronicles: Medieval, as players explore the map to gather resources and build up the strength of their army. This is done in part by exploring settlements and getting quests from NPCs, who can give tasks like clearing bandit camps or other activities. You play as legendary swordsman Miyamoto Musashi as you traverse a dark fantasy take on Kyoto, facing rival samurai, demons, and even more threats that the full game will offer. Even though it’s a 25-year-old series, with the last entry launching back in 2006, there’s no requirement to play previous games. Capcom has already said that Way of the Sword is a fresh starting point for newcomers. I was surprised by how weighty the combat felt, even with the initial bouts focused on teaching me the ropes and taking me from terrible to somewhat okay. Musashi’s prowess with a sword makes the gameplay flow naturally from one attack to the next, but it doesn’t feel like he’s moving around like Dante from Devil May Cry. Instead, every one-handed slash and cathartic two-handed hit have the weight they deserve, making dealing with crowds even more satisfying. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_rpyWOiHkAg It’s even more exciting when you eventually deplete an enemy’s stamina, whether through a flurry of sword strikes, well-timed parries, or the tuck-and-roll of a dodge. As you slowly whittle down your enemies until they’re exhausted, you can use a break to dismember them, sending the demons back to their shadowy graves and, of course, looking awesome while doing it. Despite offering plenty of different mechanics for dealing with Musashi’s enemies, the game doesn’t feel overwhelming. The demo has done exactly what it should: It sold me on Capcom’s next title. gamespot.com/articles/sonys-digital-game.title: Sony’s Digital Game Ownership Argument Is Another Attack On Consumer Rights
gamespot.com/articles/sonys-digital-game.excerpt: As Sony marches towards its all-digital future , the company is now arguing in a class-action lawsuit that it doesn't mislead customers into purchasing digital licenses for games, instead of actual ownership of the product. In a filing in California's Northern District Court made last month (and spotted by Game File ), Sony claims that "reasonable consumers would not be misled" when shopping on its storefront. The court overseeing the case against Sony is currently evaluating whether it should proceed to arbitration, as plaintiffs argue that Sony doesn't properly disclose the nature of digital purchases on its platforms. California law requires a warning label that clearly communicates to consumers of digital goods that the products they're purchasing are, in fact, digital licenses. For PlayStation games, Sony says that its terms and services disclaimer--the wall of text that accompanies a sale--lays out the nature of a purchase. The disclaimer isn't found anywhere during the purchase process; instead, Sony leaves a paragraph of text above the "confirm purchase" button. Users then need to navigate through the terms of service menus and read through the text, which includes the following line in the PlayStation 5 System Software Licence Agreement: Always read the fine print. "If you are in North America, South America, or Central America, all games and other software made available for use with your PS5 system are licensed to you, not sold, pursuant to the Software Product License Agreement." "In the digital age, it is not plausible to allege that reasonable consumers believed they were obtaining 'ownership' of a digital game," Sony's lawyers wrote in the company's defense (via Aftermath ). While Sony is correct that it does have disclaimers, this paints a worrying picture for the future of console games when there are no physical options available. gamespot.com/articles/star-wars-zero-com.title: Star Wars Zero Company Developers Were Furloughed Before The Game Even Released
gamespot.com/articles/star-wars-zero-com.excerpt: A new report has revealed that most of the Star Wars Zero Company development team at Bit Reactor was furloughed before the game launched on August 28. While the new XCOM-like Star Wars strategy game garnered positive reviews , Bit Reactor confirmed to Game File that the studio had furloughed workers in August, with a separate source suggesting that around 80% of the Zero Company's development team was impacted by this. Sources also revealed the game was developed on a very tight $50 million budget, which appeared to run out just before release and meant developers couldn't even do things like add more lightsaber animations into the game. Furloughs differ from layoffs. That means the impacted Zero Company developers are unpaid right now, with the hopes of bringing them back on and paying them again in the future, rather than being completely let go by Bit Reactor.  The path forward for the studio isn't a simple one, though, as the Game File report also uncovered that co-founders Greg Foertsch and Alison Kelly are currently embroiled in a lawsuit. Documents for that lawsuit reveal that Zero Company started life as an Apex Legends game pitch, but Respawn ultimately asked them to make it a Star Wars game. While Bit Reactor went to work on Zero Company in 2021, by 2024, Kelly claims she was being excluded from meetings and locked out of tools she needed to do her job as COO. Kelly also claims Foertsch "denied her access to books, awarded himself financial benefits, and wrongly terminated her employment." By the time Zero Company launched last month, it appears Bit Reactor ran out of money had furloughed workers as a result. That trial is scheduled to begin sometime early next year, but it is unclear if Bit Reactor will be able to financially recover and start paying its developers again. Regardless, this a disappointing turn of events happeneing at a time when the developers and players should be celebrating Star Wars Zero Company's launch .

gamespot.com/articles/paradoxs-new-grand.title: Paradox’s New Grand Strategy Game Is More Survival-RPG Than You’d Expect
gamespot.com/articles/paradoxs-new-grand.excerpt: There's no denying that Afterworld is a traditional grand strategy game in many ways--big foggy maps, territorial clashes, macro and micro decision-making--but its end-of-the-world scenario presents an opportunity for Paradox Studios to elevate the genre further still. Even in the brief glimpse we had during a hands-on play session at Gamescom, a number of differences are already showing. For a start, Afterworld has a very clear focus on lore-building, which is something the more historical games often take for granted. If you're playing as a Roman General or a post-industrial capitalist, the player tends to know what happened before that point, as a rough approximation of historical events can be summed up in an info screen before moving on. Afterworld is very clearly the outlier: Taking place some 100 years after a mysterious fictional apocalyptic event known only as The Fall, there's a lot to unpack. When you start the game, you're given a vague choice of how you'd like to conduct yourself during the early hours of the campaign. For the demo, we were the de facto leader of a band of newly emerged vault citizens (where have we heard that before?) and our reactor was about to explode. A ranger was quickly sent into the fog beyond, and our people moved a safe distance away from what was about to be a very smoky hole in the ground. There are other beginnings to choose from, but the game offers seemingly endless chances to change who you are as you live through its various terrors and triumphs. The beginning is not as important as what you choose to do next. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9PU1e7kfkfs Instead of traditional nations, you'll have bands, tribes of people with established belief systems and leaders--some friends, some foes, some undecided and purely mercenary. gamespot.com/articles/dlss-5s-leak-has-l.title: DLSS 5’s Leak Has Led To Horrific Results, But Our Demo Showed A Different Reality
gamespot.com/articles/dlss-5s-leak-has-l.excerpt: It's been a frustrating few days as someone who saw Nvidia's DLSS 5 demonstration at Gamescom last week. Since a recent mod leaked that showed DLSS 5 adjusting some characters in a pretty confusing manner, I've been under embargo and unable to discuss the true functionality, or intent, of the AI-powered filter. First teased back in March 2026, the feature received a largely negative reception due to the stark differences in character models, with some claiming they were "unrecognizable." To address the elephant in the room--yes, some of the DLSS 5-infused creations are horrific. Final Fantasy's Cloud looks like something straight out of a horror game , while adding multiple layers of DLSS 5 has made characters from The Legend of Heroes series look utterly harrowing . But from my time with Nvidia at Gamescom, I'm trying to be realistic about the use and power of the feature. Different models will produce different outputs. "DLSS 5 is intended to be used for photorealistic situations and characters," Edward Liu, Nvidia’s director of applied deep learning research said at the demo. That means no Final Fantasy, no Kingdom Hearts, and nothing that would stylistically suffer as a result of implementing it. What's more, developers can opt in or out of using the AI-powered tool, and there's more customization than just "on" or "off." Developers can create masks and adjust the filter's intensity. For example, developers can create masks in their games to ensure DLSS 5 is only applied to those areas. If you just want to enhance the appearance of food in a game, that's possible. If you're just looking to make the foliage and plants look better, that's okay too. The intensity of the filter is completely customizable by the developer. rockpapershotgun.com/the-witcher-3-songs.title: The Witcher 3: Songs of Past looked alright in its behind-closed-doors preview, though I'm more enticed by the remaster’s combat upgrades
rockpapershotgun.com/the-witcher-3-songs.excerpt: Well, I say behind-closed-doors. It turns out that if I wanted to watch a prerecorded saunter through a chunk of The Witcher III: Wild Hunt ’s Songs of the Past expansion , I could have just tuned into the Gamescom livestream , rather than travelling to Germany before parking myself in an almost pitch-black miniature theatre for 45 minutes. Now my by-touch handwritten notes are completely illegible, and I don’t even get to feel smug about attending a super secret preview. Still, the preview – which like Songs of the Past itself, was a joint operation between CD Projekt Red and co-devs Fool’s Theory – didn’t show off the expansion alone. It also focused repeatedly on the combat, movement, UI and role-playing reworks being introduced in the base game’s Remastered upgrade , which is coming months ahead of Songs of the Past on September 29th. And, usual hands-off disclaimers applying, looks like it could be the more appealing package for lapsed Witchers – especially as it’s free to owners of the original. Read more

Big Walk is strictly a co-op game, playable by as few as two players and up to 12 players, with proximity chat being a huge pillar of the game’s design. With that in mind, I reckon many people will be turned off by Big Walk, especially if you don’t have a dedicated squad to play it with. As a number of lawsuits try to take Sony to court over its decision to stop making PlayStation discs from January 2028, the platform holder has responded to one and said "reasonable consumers" understand they're only buying a license to play a game, and that they don't actually own it. This stems from a court appearance in California, where four people took Sony to court over claims the PS Store does not make it clear you're purchasing video game licenses instead of actually owning them yourself. gamespot.com/articles/sony-to-pay-out-ne.title: Sony To Pay Out Nearly $8 Million In Class-Action Settlement Over Game Prices
gamespot.com/articles/sony-to-pay-out-ne.excerpt: Sony is set to pay out nearly $8 million to PlayStation customers as part of a settlement regarding digital game prices. The settlement ( via IGN ) comes after Sony's motion to dismiss the lawsuit was denied, and settlement class members across a more-than-four-year period are potentially eligible for a payment. The lawsuit, originally filed back in 2024 , alleged that Sony established a monopoly over PlayStation Store prices by making publishers "cede control over the final price to Sony" and that Sony "eliminated the last vestiges of price competition when it stopped allowing outside retailers to sell digital download codes that could be redeemed on the PlayStation Store." Sony is not agreeing to wrongdoing as part of the settlement, and will be avoiding a civil trial if the terms are agreed upon by the court. Once that happens, the claims against Sony will be dismissed "with prejudice," meaning another lawsuit on the subject cannot be filed. You are potentially eligible for a payout if you purchased one of the affected games via the PlayStation Store between April 1, 2019 and December 31, 2023. Dozens of games are listed in the official court documents, including Nier: Automata, Resident Evil 4, The Last of Us Remastered, and Vita games like Uncharted: Golden Abyss and Killzone: Mercenary.

gamespot.com/articles/releasing-cyberpun.title: Releasing Cyberpunk 2077 In Its Poor State “Was For Sure Wrong,” CD Projekt Admits
gamespot.com/articles/releasing-cyberpun.excerpt: CD Projekt Red's RPG Cyberpunk 2077 infamously launched in December 2020 in such a poor technical state that Sony took the rare move to remove it from the PlayStation Store. Thousands of people refunded the game . CD Projekt joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski has now reflected on this, saying it "was for sure wrong" to launch the game in that state, but he pushed back against the theory that the studio did so to appease investors who wanted to see financial returns. Speaking to The Game Business , Nowakowski said COVID "was a factor" in the game's rough state at launch, because "the  team was getting exhausted in a different way." He admitted there were "people outside telling us we should launch," and fans lobbied for this as well. The developers themselves also "wanted to push it out the door" because the ongoing development was "really tiring." Looking back on it, now with the benefit of hindsight, Nowakowski said, "The decision to launch was for sure wrong, period. There is no denying it." That being said, Nowakowski said, "There were no magical investors telling us, 'You have to get this out.'" Instead, he said, "It was much more complicated and psychological." A scene from Cyberpunk 2077. CD Projekt's fiscal years follow the calendar and end on December 31. Cyberpunk 2077 was released on December 10 in 2020, and this timing led people to wonder if the developer put the game out then instead of delaying to 2021 to meet the fiscal deadline. There is, after all, precedent for game developers pushing games out the door in a rough state to hit certain fiscal deadlines. Cyberpunk 2077 might have released in a rough technical state, but it was a smashing success at launch commercially. The game sold nearly 14 million copies right out of the gate, which made it one of the most successful RPG releases in the history of video games . gamespot.com/articles/metroidvania-still.title: Metroidvania Still Feels Like A Niche Genre That Deserves Better
gamespot.com/articles/metroidvania-still.excerpt: The original Metroid and Castlevania both turn 40 years old this fall. As the two series most responsible for creating the “metroidvania,” we’re taking this occasion to take a comprehensive view of the popular genre. This is Metroidvania Week . Within the vast and overcrowded Steam store, there are over 3,100 titles with the “metroidvania” tag . Last year, Hollow Knight: Silksong accomplished a rare feat for an indie game, crashing storefronts upon its launch . And later this year, one of the genre’s namesakes is making a comeback in the form of the 2D action game Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse. And yet, 40 years after the release of the original Metroid and Castlevania games, the genre influenced by those two beloved franchises still feels relatively obscure. The metroidvania or “search-action” genre has long felt like a middle child among the wider family of (arguably arbitrary) game classifications. For whatever reason, much of the gaming industry--particularly at the AAA level--seem hesitant to try their hands with entries to the metroidvania canon the same way they do with other budding genres. The "metroidvania" tag on Steam is packed Pick any time period in the history of games and you’ll recall moments when certain types of games were all the rage. From the cartoon-mascot platformers that plagued consoles in response to Mario and Sonic, to every publisher pushing out a “Halo killer,” and PUBG triggering an onslaught of battle royales, so many genres had their moment. The list goes on, particularly for subgenres spawning from specific games--your souls-likes, roguelikes, and such. Metroid and Castlevania each underwent early peaks and long periods of radio silence. After Super Metroid--which set the template for metroidvanias that came after--a long drought followed, with Fusion and the Prime games reviving the brand, and stinkers like Other M beginning another dark era until MercurySteam’s Samus Returns and Dread. gamespot.com/articles/metroidvania-games.title: Metroidvania Games Were The Original Open-World Games
gamespot.com/articles/metroidvania-games.excerpt: The original Metroid and Castlevania both turn 40 years old this fall. As the two series most responsible for creating the “metroidvania,” we’re taking this occasion to take a comprehensive view of the popular genre. This is Metroidvania Week . When many people pick up a controller to play a game, they're looking for one thing above all others: escapism. A break from the real world. There's no better way to do that than to immerse yourself in another world. Getting lost in a completely fictional world is true escapism. These days, open-world games like Cyberpunk 2077, Red Dead Redemption 2, and the most recent Legend of Zelda games do a lot of the work here, giving us maps full of icons to wade through. But the original escapist games came in the form of search-action games, colloquially known as metroidvania games by their fans. The term metroidvania has been around since the early 2000s, and mashes together the names of two games that established the tropes of the genre early on, Metroid and Castlevania. A classic metroidvania game drops you at the entrance to an environment that feels massive (especially in the opening hours) and gives you a pretty straightforward quest like "defeat Dracula"--and then throws countless roadblocks in your path on the way to that goal (locked doors, impassable areas, area bosses), forcing you to crisscross a growing map of different, visually distinct areas, often with their own enemies and thematically appropriate challenges. Animal Well, a densely packed metroidvania Those roadblocks are key to making the exploration feel like it matters. You can't go anywhere you like at the beginning; you'll need to unlock ways to open doors and new movement options to let you bypass hazards. When you eventually get through that barrier and into a new biome, that sense of wonder at seeing a new place can set in. The campaign's had a chilling effect, leaving developers making games including any sexual content in a kind of limbo as to whether digital storefronts will host their work. gamespot.com/articles/you-can-watch-a-co.title: You Can Watch A Cow Play Eve Online Right Now
gamespot.com/articles/you-can-watch-a-co.excerpt: Earlier this summer, Fenris Creations (formerly CCP Games) released an update to its popular online spacefaring MMO called Cradle of War, which the community immediately abbreviated to "CoW." This shorthand apparently sparked a few ideas inside Fenris, and now an actual cow is livestreaming an Eve Online session from Iceland. The cow, whose name is Valva and username is FC CapitalCowPilot, is manning a mining ship on a deep space mining operation. The team at Fenris Creations fitted its pen with "cow-proof" buttons, which when stepped on will perform certain in-game actions, while a voiceover host delivers cow facts to viewers of the livestream. https://bsky.app/profile/lotrlore.bsky.social/post/3muk2ibt4zk25 As of this writing, over 200 players have joined CapitalCowPilot's mining expedition, with over 4000 viewers watching along on Twitch as the cow moves around its pen. Fenris Creations has announced some community goals which can be unlocked during the stream, including new skins for ships and new updates for the Cradle of War expansion. The stream will run "for roughly 4 to 6 hours," as Fenris admits that it's "on the cow's time, she's not on ours." Valva has made quite an impression on the stream's chat, with some users demanding that the cow be left alone while on its mining mission. The Cradle of War expansion's non-bovine additions include time-limited Military Campaigns, which let players complete tasks in order to advance their empire's goals, and a new area called Exordium specifically built to help onboard new players.

gamespot.com/articles/super-smash-bros-u.title: Super Smash Bros. Ultimate Gets An Update, But Not The One You Want
gamespot.com/articles/super-smash-bros-u.excerpt: In what feels like a monkey's paw situation, Super Smash Bros. Ultimate unexpectedly received a new patch--but unlike recent updates for other major Nintendo games, this Smash update doesn't include any Switch 2-specific features. The Ver. 13.0.5 patch for Ultimate fixes "behavior that occurs when invalid data is sent or received in online battles," according to the Nintendo Support website . It isn't clear from the patch notes (or note, rather) what "invalid data" refers to, but some users on Reddit speculated that the update targets mods. Meanwhile, fellow Switch 1 game Mario Kart 8 Deluxe received a hefty 4.0.0 update with substantial features for Switch 2 users, including split-screen support for up to eight players, camera support, shorter loading times, and higher resolutions. Pikmin 3 Deluxe also got a similar Switch 2 update this week. It's a disappointing time for Smash Bros. fans, with not a single hint of a new Smash game or a proper Switch 2 update for Ultimate, whether that comes in the form of a free patch or a Switch 2 Edition with new content. There's a laundry list of features that players would love to see in a Switch 2 version of Smash Bros. Ultimate , including new characters, additional stages, increased resolution, and implementation of rollback netcode. The only Switch 2-related update that Ultimate received came in June 2025 , fixing an issue where online matches with Mii Fighters would end immediately if one of the players was playing on a Switch 2. Development for new content ended in 2021 after the addition of Sora from Kingdom Hearts capped off Ultimate's DLC. The latest title from Smash Bros. creator Masahiro Sakurai is Kirby Air Riders, which launched last November with no DLC planned . Perhaps Smash fans should bet on a new Smash game coming instead of an Ultimate update, though we can probably all agree that Sakurai deserves a break . It’s Time For Smash Bros. gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-morality-sys.excerpt: Grand Theft Auto 6 is looking to add some extra wrinkles to several of its established gameplay pillars, but the biggest update here might just be the inclusion of an honor system. Taking a page from Red Dead Redemption 2, GTA 6 will remind you that actions have consequences, as your less-than-legal activities will feed into a criminal profile that evolves with you. Not only are there various profiles within this that gauge just how effective you are at crime--or bloodthirsty--but developer Rockstar Games will let you break it entirely if you cause too much chaos. "There's no right or wrong way to play the game," GTA 6 co-head of development Rob Nelson said to YouTuber TGG. "Just a bit more choice now. How do you want to play this game if your actions may have some impact on things? You can still cause as much chaos as you want if that's what you want to do. I don't think it changes what GTA is. It changes what it can be for people who want to engage with it in that way. You still have as much freedom as you had before; you can just do more now, and you have more choice in terms of how you approach situations." https://youtu.be/33t4kUEBL5k At the highest level, players can have a criminal record that labels them as a "Professional," and from there, the states descend into Aggressive, Violent, and Psycho. Reaching the fifth, currently unnamed state, is said to be particularly tough, but once you do, there's no return from a full descent into villainy. The idea is that players will have the freedom to alternate between criminal profiles or replay the game while aiming to align with those particular states. Players can also disable notifications about their profile status changing, and the co-protagonists Jason and Lucia will each have their own profile that changes throughout the course of the game depending on the actions you take with them. gamespot.com/articles/sony-warns-playsta.title: Sony Warns PlayStation Customers Against Harassing Support Staff Amid Disc Backlash
gamespot.com/articles/sony-warns-playsta.excerpt: Sony's decision to kill off PlayStation game discs has been met with almost universal disdain since it was first announced, and it looks like its employees have been caught in the crossfire. Just about every Sony announcement or social media post is met with calls for it to reverse its decision, and Sony Japan has instituted a new anti-harassment policy to protect the customer service employees who have had to deal with a vocal contingent of dissatisfied consumers. These changes also align with new workplace laws in Japan that will take effect later this year. "Similar to other companies in Japan, Sony Interactive Entertainment has published its policy in compliance with a new law taking effect on October 1, which requires employers in Japan to implement measures to address customer harassment," Sony said in response to GameSpot. According to the policy , Sony will restrict people who "exceed what is considered reasonable" when interacting with customer service, including "unreasonable demands" for compensation or apologies. Abusive language, threats, and "forcing someone to prostrate themselves" can also get you cut off from the help desk, as will visiting offices or related facilities without permission. Sony added that it will work with the police and lawyers, if necessary, to protect its employees. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4FatSqS3VYY&t=19s&pp=0gcJCRoMAYcqIYzv While customer service workers are currently dealing with backlash over Sony's decision to focus on an all-digital future, the company has also been criticized for several more recent actions. Sony responded to a class action lawsuit in which it was accused of not clearly informing consumers that its digital store sells game licenses, not full games. Various publishers have also accused Sony of anti-competitive moves and of working toward creating a monopoly through its digital storefront. Sony will pay out nearly $8 million to PlayStation customers as part of a settlement over digital game prices.

gamespot.com/articles/lego-skylines-is-m.title: Lego Skylines Is More Than Just A Lego Skin On A Familiar Game
gamespot.com/articles/lego-skylines-is-m.excerpt: Our hands-on preview of Lego Skylines at Gamescom quickly allayed any fears that Paradox's new city builder would just be Cities Skylines with a fun new skin. It's so much more than a glorified DLC. This is undoubtedly its own game, something shaped from the ground up to be both a solid city-builder from a recognized name and a charming Lego game with all the trademark humor and tactile brick action. You start by choosing your avatar from a selection of Lego mini figures, making you a tangible character in their world, and you're soon tasked with building a home. Crucially, though, you're not zoning residential areas--you are literally building one home. For a family of real brick-based guys with real needs and wants and desires. In this case my Lego family wished for a garden gnome to be placed outside their house, which I was easy enough to fulfill. Houses are selected from menus first by size and then by appearance. Each house of the same size is functionally the same, but you can choose if you'd like a sleek, flat-roofed city pad or a rustic farmstead, for example. A family will eventually move in and the house type will help dictate what kind of environment they want around their house. Decor--which ranges from plaza fountains to big colorful slides or food trucks--can be placed in square panels around houses, reflecting "flavors" like cozy, traditional, or modern. You're encouraged to choose what the families have asked for to increase your Appeal Level, but there's no fail state if you prioritize aesthetics over practicality. Creating workplaces is crucial to Happiness, taxes, and resource chains. Each house, decor patch, workplace, shop, etc, all also have customization menus, which open up the real granular creativity that fans of Lego are likely to crave. Every detail is down to you--whether you want to change the color palette of the roof, or the type of flowers on the lawn, maybe you want to install a wood shed, or give them a teeny-tiny garden bench. gamespot.com/articles/tomb-raider-legacy.excerpt: I know Lara Croft well. At least, I feel like I do. You see, we've grown up together. From the original Tomb Raider games, I was hooked. As a young girl, I had an insatiable sense of wonder following Lara's adventures, and as a teen I was enthused when Crystal Dynamics took over development and rescued Lara from Core Design's clutches back in 2007. I even remained on board for the series reboot in 2013, although my interest in the titular tomb raider had waned slightly. At the time, I was most keen to see how Lara fit into the gaming world almost 20 years on from her debut, and I came away feeling like she was the most realistic version of herself she had ever been--initially frightened and vulnerable, but honing her skills and gaining experience as the reboot trilogy progressed. Now, with an extra decade under her belt (and mine), Lara Croft is returning to her roots with a reimagining of her classic adventures that has me feeling pretty skeptical. I'm excited for another title in a franchise I adore, yet concerned that I was pretty happy with Lara's origin story, and rehashing it once more could tarnish that experience. The original Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis announcement left me feeling conflicted. It seemed like the intent was to unify all of the versions of Lara that we've come to know over the years, yet it felt limiting to do that in the form of a reboot of the original game. The new environments are Legacy of Atlantis' strongest point. By the time I got to my Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis preview at Gamescom, though, I was feeling optimistic. From the trailers and sneak peeks I'd seen so far, Lara was looking better than ever, and the nostalgia value added to my eager anticipation. Unfortunately, nothing I saw during that preview event excited me. The most intriguing element of the preview content I saw was the way Crystal Dynamics has rebuilt and reimagined the environments. gamespot.com/articles/resident-evil-dire.excerpt: Resident Evil games over the years have slowly added more fantastical elements to their tale of bioweapons running amok, but for the new live-action movie , director Zach Cregger is dialing back those ideas to a more "grounded" level. Even so, he doesn't think he'd fare very well if he were dropped in that world. "I feel like some of the Resident Evil games get a little magical," Cregger said during a Reddit Ask Me Anything session (via YouTuber Troy Hill Talks Movies ). "[Resident Evil] 8, we have a woman who can turn into a bird and fly around. And like, I love it. I've played it a bunch of times. I think it's an awesome game, but in terms of me making a movie out of it, it's like I've got to try and limit some of the wild aspects of Resident Evil. And so I chose to stick with the T-Virus, keep it as grounded as possible. So that means I'm not going to have a gigantic jacked dude in a trench coat, because I'm like, where'd the coat come from? How did he get the coat?" https://youtu.be/mNd1gb19A-c Cregger explained that while the Resident Evil games do explain how Mr. X gets his stylish coat, in the world he has constructed for the movie, there's no time for the infected bioweapons to consider zombie apocalypse fashion. "This movie, it's like the outbreak just happened," Cregger added. "I want to keep it chaotic, I want to keep it primal, and I want to just keep it as grounded as I can. The T-Virus causes all kinds of cool, fun mutations. That is enough, so I'm limiting it there." As a co-founder of the comedy troupe The Whitest Kids U' Know, Cregger says that the muscles he developed for creating sketch comedy also helped him zero in on "absurd" opportunities and find the right timing for unexpected results in Resident Evil. As for his chances of surviving his own creation? Cregger doesn't think he'd last too long in his version of Resident Evil. gamespot.com/articles/this-horror-game-i.title: This Horror Game Is Having A Dino Crisis Of A Different Sort
gamespot.com/articles/this-horror-game-i.excerpt: Athanasia , the indie horror game that traps you in a mysterious facility full of dinosaurs, is launching in the ideal horror-game window: just before Halloween. GameSpot can exclusively reveal Athanasia's release date; it comes to PC on October 19 via Steam Early Access. In Athanasia, players find themselves trapped in a South American research facility swarmed by dinosaurs that have somehow traveled through time to the present day in the game's story. Though the art style recalls something quite like Dino Crisis, Capcom's long-dormant dino horror series, the specifics of the gameplay are actually more surprising. Influenced by System Shock, the first-person Athanasia also has immersive-sim leanings, as seen in the game's trailer below, where the player can creatively get themselves out of a jam by experimenting with their environment. Of course, if it's really an immersive sim, players will be able to flush the toilets. It's wait-and-see on that one. That's not the only wrinkle, though. Athanasia also teases a different enemy type hidden from all of the game's trailers so far. It seems something worse than dinosaurs is lurking. Athanasia launches on October 19 from Momentum Games, with the horror-focused Black Lantern Collective publishing.

gamespot.com/articles/how-the-resident-e.title: How The Resident Evil Movie Borrows From RE4 And RE7
gamespot.com/articles/how-the-resident-e.excerpt: Ahead of the release of Resident Evil later this month, director Zach Cregger sat down for an Ask Me Anything session on Reddit he answered questions about the movie. While trailers for Resident Evil have teased a few Easter eggs that players of the game will recognize, Cregger also spoke about another game-inspired influence on his horror movie: Resident Evil's third-person viewpoint. "I feel like the biggest inspiration for this was the games, and I mean cinematically," Cregger said during the AMA (via YouTuber Troy Hill Talks Movies ). "I'm not talking about the content of the movie. I'm talking about the visual language of the movie. I feel like people my age and younger, we grew up with our visual tastes informed just as much by video games as we did by movies. I know as a kid, I played video games probably just as much as I watched movies. There's something that is ingrained now about this third-person camera and this first-person thing where you really are learning the space as the character learns the space, and you feel much more immersed in their perspective because you are. And so, for me to make a movie about Resident Evil where I'm following a character on his foot journey, it's like, obviously, I'm going to employ the visual vocabulary that these games have employed so well." https://youtu.be/SJPu1spHqfk Cregger added that he choreographed scenes to emulate this gameplay approach, so as to "train the viewer" early on as to how they're going to experience the movie and the journey of Bryan, the medical courier played by Austin Abrams . Resident Evil 7 was also influential on the film for how it portrayed a normal person being put through the ringer, Cregger said, but Resident Evil 4 also played a large role in the "rhythm" of the film. gamespot.com/articles/how-40-years-of-me.title: How 40 Years of Metroid Have Impacted The Biggest Metroidvania Developers
gamespot.com/articles/how-40-years-of-me.excerpt: Metroid’s impact on the industry is widespread enough to have a whole genre named after it. It’s a privilege it splits with Castlevania, but it’s an honor all the same: a rarity shared by the likes of Rogue and Demon’s Souls. This seminal 1986 NES title helped spawn an entire style of game and influenced many creators across the industry. GameSpot spoke to various developers behind a number of modern metroidvanias to get their input on the Metroid series and how it has impacted the games they have made. These interviews have been edited for length and clarity. Rémi Boutin, senior game designer on Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown I discovered Metroid through Super Metroid, and apart from the alien atmosphere, the amazing Samus Aran, and the unforgettable intro, what immediately struck me was its interconnected world. At the time, I was playing a lot of level-based games, and having this huge, hostile maze to explore, full of mysteries and secrets to uncover, was incredible. It conveyed a thrill of adventure that I had rarely experienced before, except perhaps with Zelda. For me, this is the heart of the Metroid experience: exploring a world, then making it your own. Samus becomes stronger through upgrades, but players also become better through their knowledge of the world and their mastery of its rules. Shattering the glass tube in Brinstar with a Power Bomb after passing through it many times (and seeing another smashed tube) remains one of my most memorable gaming moments. This process of mastering the world was a major inspiration for Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown. We knew some players struggled to remember places they needed to revisit and we wanted to preserve their autonomy without letting them feel lost. Our solution is to let players “annotate” the map with screenshots to mark places to revisit later. I hope it gives players the same pleasure of exploration I felt when I first explored Zebes. gamespot.com/articles/mario-kart-8-delux.title: Mario Kart 8 Deluxe Just Got A Surprise Free Update With 8-Player Split-Screen
gamespot.com/articles/mario-kart-8-delux.excerpt: Mario Kart 8 Deluxe has been Nintendo's golden goose for several years, as it's the company's best-selling Switch game of all time and has received various updates over the years, becoming a feature-packed experience. Even with Mario Kart World aiming to usurp its position, Nintendo isn't done dropping new content into Mario Kart 8 yet, as the game just received a new eight-player split-screen mode out of nowhere on Switch 2. It's free to download, allows for up to eight players to share the screen locally, and it looks wild in action. Alongside the new mode that segments your TV like a slab of chocolate, Mario Kart 8 Deluxe Version 4.0.0 also adds several more improvements that take advantage of the increased horsepower on Switch 2. In a nutshell, you're getting sharper graphics, CameraPlay support, and shorter load times in addition to smaller quality-of-life tweaks under the hood of the popular kart-racing game. Even player speed has been increased by a whopping coin--whatever that means. https://twitter.com/NintendoAmerica/status/2094968553728274749 But the expanded local split-screen is the real star of the show here, as not only can you strain your eyes while playing on TV, but you can also make your local optometrist happy by watching all those races unfold in handheld mode on the Switch 2. Considering just how much of an intensive load it is to render eight sessions in real time, the new multiplayer mode is a technical marvel to watch. This will likely keep Mario Kart 8 Deluxe at the top of the Nintendo food chain for a while yet. Mario Kart World has its charm, but as fans have pointed out, the anemic amount of content added since its launch last year has made it hard to root for. That drought might be coming to a temporary end, as with a rumored Nintendo Direct supposedly arriving later this month, players are expecting Mario Kart World to get some sort of an update.
